newsitem.title: UK: ENGLISH SOCCER MATCH-RIGGING TRIAL BEGINS.
newsitem.headline: ENGLISH SOCCER MATCH-RIGGING TRIAL BEGINS.

text.p: Former Liverpool goalkeeper Bruce Grobbelaar was accused on Tuesday of taking large sums of money to rig top soccer games in England for the benefit of an Asian gambling syndicate.

Grobbelaar appeared on the first day of his trial at Winchester Crown Court in southern England along with fellow goalkeeper Hans Segers, former footballer John Fashanu and a Malaysian businessman, Heng Suan Lim, known as Richard Lim.
They all denied charges of conspiring to give and accept corrupt payments in order to influence first division and premier league games between February 1991 and November 1994.

In particular, Grobbelaar -- a Zimbabwean who helped Liverpool win a host of English and European competitions -- denies taking 40,000 pounds ($66,900) to influence the outcome of a Liverpool game against Newcastle in November 1993.
"Mr Grobbelaar has admitted to the crime on tape and video, and was party to such an agreement," prosecutor David Calvert Smith told the court.
The allegations of match-fixing erupted in the media in November, 1994.

Calvert Smith said Lim was "an associate by telephone with Mr Grobbelaar" and was responsible for handing over money to the former Liverpool goalkeeper, whose antics during 13 years with Liverpool earned him the nickname "clown prince of soccer".
Calvert Smith began his opening statement by giving the members of the jury hefty dossiers containing details of telephone calls made by the defendants and of their bank accounts.
"A great deal turns on telephone contact in this case," he told the jury.
Calvert Smith said members of the jury might wonder how one player could alone ensure the result desired by gamblers.
"Well, of course, he can't. He may not have the opportunity to do so," the prosecutor said, noting that his own defenders or the opposing team could foil his attempts.
"That is exactly what happened in a game between Liverpool and Manchester United in January 1994, about which you will hear a good deal," he said.
But goalkeepers were the obvious players to tap, for people seeking to influence a game corruptly, Calvert Smith said.
"Goalkeepers do make a mistake sometimes, so it may be that the odd deliberate mistake may escape attention," he added.

Grobbelaar left Liverpool in August, 1994, for Southampton, another English premier league club, but now plays for Plymouth in the second division. Fashanu and Segers played for Wimbledon in the premier league. Lim was a former accountancy student, involved in buying and selling Mercedes-Benz cars in Britain. He also had an interest in a London restaurant during the period, Calvert Smith said.
"Mr Fashanu was an associate of Mr Segers and of Mr Lim and was in receipt of large sums of money, unexplained in terms of his known pursuits at the time, from Indonesia," Calvert Smith said.
The defendants arrived at the court on Tuesday morning looking relaxed, smiling and chatting with friends and reporters before the case began.
The prosecution's unfolding of the charges is expected to take two days, and the trial judge, Justice Simon Tuckey, said the case was likely to take eight weeks, until March 11.
"It may last a bit longer than that but I think everyone is confident it will finish before Easter, which is at the end of March," Tuckey said. ($1=.5979 Pound)
